_comment: PINNED source of truth for the 5-platform JDK 25 installer coordinates. The ONLY file the maintainer edits (version + url) when a vendor ships a newer JDK 25 build. :jdk-downloader downloads each 'url'; the installer-gen resolver fetches each 'sha256Url' from the VENDOR, verifies the downloaded bytes against it (a mismatch = corrupt download OR a newer build shipped -> fix the pin by hand), INFERS javaHomeSubpath from the real archive, and GENERATES website/installer/jdk-coordinates.json (a build output, not committed). NO sha256 is hardcoded here — it is downloaded from the vendor so download correctness is validated, not asserted against a stale literal. vendor: corretto | azul-zulu | microsoft. sha256Url body: corretto = bare 64-hex; azul-zulu = JSON with 'sha256_hash'; microsoft = '.sha256sum.txt' (sha + filename). Vendor asymmetry: Corretto's latest_sha256 alias tracks the LATEST build, so a mismatch also signals 'a newer JDK 25 shipped — bump version+url'; Azul's UUID-pinned detail URL never drifts, so an Azul mismatch means corruption only (bump Azul version+url+uuid by hand). format: zip | tar.gz | tar.xz. javaHomeSubpath is intentionally absent — inferred by the generator.
